items.description: A tall granite obelisk in Montevideo commemorating the hundredth anniversary of the first Uruguayan Constitution. It stands at the end of the 18 de Julio avenue.
A historic harbor market building featuring an intricate iron structure brought from England in the 19th century. Today it is famous for its traditional parrilla restaurants.
An iconic wavy bridge in La Barra known for its distinctive curved design. It was engineered to cross the Maldonado River and is a recognized architectural symbol of the area.
A modern commercial complex in the Buceo district representing the financial heart of the capital. Its towers are a hallmark of the city's growing business sector.
A state-of-the-art multifunctional indoor arena in Montevideo, opened in 2018. It hosts major sporting events, concerts, and conventions.
A prominent lighthouse in the upscale village of José Ignacio. It serves as a navigational aid and a landmark for the coastal tourism area.
A luxurious mansion that now functions as a museum of decorative arts. It was built for the Ortiz de Taranco family in the early 20th century.
An exquisite 19th-century palace that previously served as the presidential residence. It currently houses the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The longest mountain range in Uruguay, extending across the northern part of the country. It serves as a major watershed for surrounding river systems.
A small mountain chain characterized by its rugged peaks and beautiful scenery. It is a popular destination for hikers and nature lovers.
